transcript:
Header: Recorded 2025-04-11 15:00 PDT | Duration 75m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Acme CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of ML Infra), Sara Gomez (Security)

Summary (auto): discuss on-prem air-gapped artifact delivery, offline licensing mechanics, GPU driver dependencies, container runtime notes (docker/nvidia-container-toolkit vs singularity), and benchmark plan for KV cache/batching/quantization.

00:00:01 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the account lead on this. uh ethan from our infra team will run the deep dive. welcome.
00:00:08 Priya Singh: thanks maya, appreciate it. we're hoping to get clarity on how the artifact gets to our airgapped site and how licensing works offline.
00:00:18 Ethan Park: yep, great. quick agenda — artifact packaging and delivery, offline license format and activation semantics, driver/runtime matrix, and then benchmark scripts for latency/throughput focusing on kv cache and batching.
00:00:30 Liam O'Connor: perfect. i want to make sure quantization paths are supported — we plan to run int8 on some nodes for cost reasons.
00:00:37 Ethan Park: totally, we'll cover quantization profiles and how we ship quantized model variants, and the expected perf delta.
00:00:45 Sara Gomez: quick security note — we need to understand checksums, signing, and any license activation phone-home behavior. air-gapped = zero egress.
00:00:55 Maya Chen: yep, our offline licensing is whitelist-based, there is no outbound heartbeat required by default; there is an opt-in periodic verification if customers want to enable telemetry but for enterprises we ship a signed license token that the runtime validates locally.
00:01:12 Priya Singh: is that HSM-backed or just a file?
00:01:16 Maya Chen: typically it's a signed license file (json blob with signature) which you can store in an HSM or KMS if you want. for stronger setups we support an enterprise activation package that can be imported via our CLI.
00:01:33 Ethan Park: (slight pause) okay i'm going to share the artifact layout — imagine a tarball: onprem_artifacts/acme-202504.tar.gz — inside it's containers/, drivers/, models/, runbooks/, checksums/ with sha256 files. we'll include an offline license file and a JSON manifest.
00:01:54 Maya Chen: note: the manifest also contains kernel hints for fastest paths (fp16 vs int8) and recommended batching profiles based on observed sequence length.
00:02:05 Liam O'Connor: can you re-say the driver bit — we run RHEL 8.6 and some nodes are airgapped with older kernels. nv driver versions are sensitive.
00:02:13 Ethan Park: yeah — we'll provide a driver compatibility matrix: driver package (rpm), expected kernel module version, supported cuda version, and recommended nvidia-container-toolkit version. for very locked-down hosts we'll also provide an OCI image that already includes the runtime, so minimal host deps.
00:02:31 Sara Gomez: does the artifact include the nvidia driver? that has licensing implications for us.
00:02:35 Ethan Park: we do not ship proprietary vendor drivers by default — we ship the recommended package names and checksums and a driver-install helper script. in special cases we can package vendor driver binaries if your legal team approves — that's a separate vendor agreement.
00:02:51 Priya Singh: ok that helps. what about the container runtime — some of our infra uses singularity instead of docker.
00:02:58 Ethan Park: singluarity/singularity-ce is fine; we provide the runtime as an OCI bundle that can be run by either docker/ctr/singularity. there may be minor entrypoint tweaks. we'll include examples for both.
00:03:15 Maya Chen: moving on to licensing semantics — offline license is bound to host identifiers (mac, machine-id, optionally TPM pubkey). it's a zero-egress validate-on-start model; runtime will refuse to start if the license doesn't match.
00:03:30 Liam O'Connor: do you support license rotation? like rotating keys in the HSM?
00:03:33 Maya Chen: yes, we support rotation via a signed rotation package. you can stage rotation artifacts in the same tarball and run the rotation tool offline.
00:03:42 Sara Gomez: can you confirm there's no fingerprinting that leaks model prompts? we need assurance that no PII leaves environment.
00:03:49 Ethan Park: correct — offline mode disables telemetry by default; logs are local and can be redirected. we do include debug bundles for troubleshooting but they are opt-in and sanitized.
00:03:59 Maya Chen: now we'll talk perf: our runtime uses KV cache for chat workloads, continuous batching for throughput. the artifact includes a benchmark harness that exercises kv cache warmup, half-precision (fp16) and int8 quantized runs, and measures latency P50/P95/P99 under different batch sizes.
00:04:20 Priya Singh: is kv cache warmup deterministic? our use-case has long context and cache sharding across GPUs.
00:04:28 Ethan Park: warmup behavior is deterministic given the same prompt history; for sharded KV across GPUs we recommend pinned mapping which we'll include in the config templates. we'll also include a tool to simulate realistic prefix cache warmups.
00:04:42 Liam O'Connor: what about memory footprint for kv cache with int8 quantized models?
00:04:46 Ethan Park: int8 reduces weight storage, but kv cache precision is usually fp16; we ship kv quantization experiments — you can do 8-bit kv in some models but it has a measurable quality delta. our benchmark harness will show expected memory and latency tradeoffs.
00:05:02 Priya Singh: can your harness run without gpu (cpu fallback) for pre-validate installs? some of our sandbox hosts lack GPUs.
00:05:07 Ethan Park: yes, we include cpu-only runner with smaller synthetic tests. runtime detects available devices and will skip gpu-specific tests.
00:05:16 Maya Chen: (interruption) quick question from lane — do we support offline telemetry bundles for debug?
00:05:21 Ethan Park: yes — customers can opt to package logs and debug traces into an encrypted tarball that they can upload to an s3 location or hand over to redwood via secure transfer. again, only if they opt-in.
00:05:32 Sara Gomez: thanks. on the install runbook — we need explicit steps for kernel module signing and secure driver installation.
00:05:38 Ethan Park: we'll add step-by-step commands for dkms vs manual insmod, and for RHEL/CentOS we'll provide rpm packages and gpg signatures.
00:05:48 Liam O'Connor: runbook should include fallback plan if driver fails — e.g., boot to rescue and blacklisting modules.
00:05:53 Ethan Park: noted, we'll include a troubleshooting appendix.
00:05:58 Maya Chen: moving to benchmarks — we'll run a small 2-node pilot in your environment: 1 infer node + 1 controller. plan is to run our benchmark harness to capture P50/P95/P99 for single-stream low-latency and multi-stream throughput with batching.
00:06:12 Priya Singh: what's the expected P95 for a 13B model with fp16 on A10 equivalent?
00:06:17 Ethan Park: ballpark: single-request P95 ~150-220ms depending on sequence length and kv warm state. with batching of 8 you see throughput improve ~6x with P95 around 400-500ms depending on concurrency. that's approximate — the harness will give numbers for your exact infra.
00:06:36 Liam O'Connor: what's the typical disk footprint for models + kv cache?
00:06:40 Ethan Park: model storage varies; a 13B fp16 model ~25-30GB, int8 quantized variant ~10-12GB. kv cache is per-token ~ (hidden_size * 2 * bytes) — in practice expect 2-5GB per 1k tokens per GPU depending on architecture. we'll include a calculator.
00:06:59 Priya Singh: good. about the artifact transfer — our security policy prefers checksum-verified USB transfer or signed ISO via courier. can you support signed ISO images?
00:07:10 Maya Chen: yes, we can produce a signed ISO with sha256 and gpg signature. we'll also provide an MD5 for legacy tools but sha256 is primary.
00:07:18 Sara Gomez: any licensing UI? our infra team wants a cli that they can run to import license.
00:07:23 Ethan Park: there is a CLI: redwood-install import-license --file license.json --host-id <id>. it validates signature and writes to /etc/redwood/license. we'll include examples for automated ansible/chef/puppet tasks.
00:07:36 Liam O'Connor: agentless install? we prefer no daemons that phone home.
00:07:40 Maya Chen: runtime runs as local process; optional orchestration agents are just helpers. nothing phones home by default in offline mode.
00:07:47 Priya Singh: what about GPU driver EULA — if you can't ship vendor driver, how will you ensure exact driver binary checksum matches?
00:07:56 Ethan Park: we'll provide exact driver package names and sha256, and if you'd like we can do a vendor-approved packaging workflow where your legal signs off and we include vendor binaries in a sealed artifact. that's handled as a special case.
00:08:11 Sara Gomez: ok. will you support airgap update process for future model rollouts? we can't re-open internet for every update.
00:08:18 Maya Chen: yes, we support delta artifacts — small patch bundles with model diffs and signed rotation files. customers can apply them via the same import CLI.
00:08:27 Liam O'Connor: let's talk about kernel modules and container runtimes — are there prebuilt kernel modules for older kernels?
00:08:33 Ethan Park: we include prebuilt kmods for common kernels (RHEL 7/8, Ubuntu 18/20/22) but for very old or custom kernels we provide dkms sources to build locally. the runbook shows how to build and sign modules.
00:08:46 Priya Singh: test plan — we'll want to run prefix-cache heavy chat tests plus high-throughput embedding workloads. do you provide embedding test vectors?
00:08:56 Ethan Park: yes, harness includes embedding microbench, batch embedding at sizes 16/64/128, and we give expected token/sec and GPU utilization patterns.
00:09:08 Maya Chen: (brief) we also include a trace plugin to collect latency traces without telemetry; it writes to local file which you can share if you choose.
00:09:17 Priya Singh: perfect. quick nit — how do you handle license binding for ephemeral VMs? we need license to move between nodes.
00:09:25 Ethan Park: we support license pooling across a cluster; you can issue a cluster license that binds to cluster-id (derived from master controller cert) rather than a single host.
00:09:36 Liam O'Connor: what about disasters and backup restore of licenses?
00:09:40 Maya Chen: the runbook includes license backup and restore steps; encrypted export/import is supported.
00:09:47 Sara Gomez: ok can we see the manifest format?
00:09:50 Ethan Park: yes — sample manifest: { "artifact_version": "1.2.0", "components": ["models/13B-fp16", "containers/runtime-1.4.0" ], "checksums": {"models/13B-fp16.bin": "sha256.." }, "drivers": [ {"name":"nvidia-driver-525", "sha256":"..."} ] }  — note: transcript may have garbled quotes here, but we'll attach the manifest in the artifact.
00:10:18 Priya Singh: sounds good. any constraints on offline licensing cryptography? we need FIPS support.
00:10:24 Maya Chen: we support FIPS mode for the runtime; signed artifacts use RSA/ECDSA options — we'll provide FIPS-compliant signing on request.
00:10:33 Ethan Park: next, deployment topology — controller handles routing and can route to dedicated infer pools. in your on-prem env we can run controller in airgapped mode; it's an admin component that doesn't require egress.
00:10:45 Liam O'Connor: how does routing fallback work if a pinned GPU pool is down?
00:10:49 Ethan Park: offline-only configs can be set to failover to a local spare pool; there's also a mode to degrade model to a smaller quantized variant if capacity constrained.
00:11:00 Priya Singh: that degrade behavior — is it automatic or manual?
00:11:03 Ethan Park: you can set automatic fallback policies in the controller config; we'll include example configs.
00:11:10 Maya Chen: (wrap) ok we're at about 11 minutes of Q/A — actually the call is 75 but this transcript includes periodic highlights; we'll capture full recording in the file we share.
00:11:20 Priya Singh: a couple final items — can you share the exact CLI commands and example ansible playbook?
00:11:25 Ethan Park: yes, example ansible role will be included in runbooks/ansible/acme-role.yml inside tarball.
00:11:32 Liam O'Connor: regarding benchmarks: please include expected GPU metrics (util, mem, sm occupancy) and scripts to collect nvidia-smi and dcgm metrics offline.
00:11:41 Ethan Park: included.
00:11:43 Sara Gomez: and include the signed iso option for transfer.
00:11:46 Maya Chen: noted.
00:11:49 Priya Singh: ok let's recap next steps.
00:11:52 Maya Chen: recap: redwood will provide artifact tarball (signed iso option), sha256, driver matrix, install runbook, ansible examples, and benchmark harness. customer to provide host inventory and confirm pilot window. we'll aim for pilot week of 2025-04-21.
00:12:08 Priya Singh: sounds good.
00:12:10 Liam O'Connor: thanks everyone.
00:12:12 Maya Chen: thanks — we'll follow up with a link in the crm and a shared s3 link for the artifact (or signed iso option). action items in crm.

Notes/misc: Transcript contains occasional misheard tokens (k-v cash vs kv cache). References: Artifact (internal link) s3://redwood-artifacts/acme/onprem_202504.tar.gz; Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/docs/onprem-runbooks/acme-example (redwood-internal); Example ansible role: runbooks/ansible/acme-role.yml

End of transcript.
